api(): same-origin fetch with JSON headers; non-2xx -> Error built from FastAPI detail (string or {message,recovery}); 401 -> window event 'hermbot-session-expired'
mutate(): attaches a stable Idempotency-Key per (method+path+body) fingerprint until success so retries of the same mutation reuse the key

functions.desc: drops all remembered idempotency keys (sign-out / session expiry)

features.title: Operational tooling (configure, upgrade, check, stop, notification keys, audits, acceptance drivers)
features.purpose: Host-side Python scripts that create and upgrade the private .env without printing secrets, run the isolated test suite in containers, stop the stack safely, generate VAPID keys, and produce/verify acceptance evidence (test-results/*.json) against the live local workspace and Docker state.

logic.step: Bootstrap: configure.py creates .env exclusively (0600) with random tokens/passwords and CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY; compose refuses to start until those exist.
Upgrade: upgrade_config.py appends CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY and PUBLIC_URL only if missing and re-chmods 0600.
Push keys: notification_setup.py --contact mailto:... generates a P-256 VAPID pair once (preserves an existing private key), then api and notification-worker must be recreated.
Checks: check.py starts postgres/storage, ensures hermbot_test, builds hermbot-tools, runs ruff and pytest (junit to test-results/backend.xml) on hermbot_control.
Stop: stop.py stops the worker first (prevents desired-state reconciliation restarting bots), then labelled managed runtimes, then all compose services; volumes preserved.

Audits (read-only): phase2/phase3/phase4, native_tools, skills_tools, work_outcomes, routines_final, routines_integrity verify saved evidence vs live API (owner Bearer token read from .env), artifact sha256, container image/volume/hardening, upstream Hermes source unchanged, and write *-audit.json proofs.

Acceptance drivers (mutating, staged): phase3_inflight, phase3_browser_persistence, phase3_recovery_driver (signal files), group_work_history (--apply), event_trigger_acceptance and event_provider_acceptance (stage argv; proof manifest guards against duplicate fixtures).

data.text: .env (owner-private secrets; created/appended/rewritten by configure/upgrade_config/notification_setup; read for OWNER_TOKEN by audits; passed to tools container by check.py).
test-results/*.json and backend.xml evidence files written by drivers/audits and read back by later audits.
Direct DB access from in-container drivers: reads of event_sources/connector_operations/trigger_* and writes in browser-cleanup and reconcile_creation.

decisions.decision: Scripts never print credential values; audits project Docker inspect output without container environments.
decisions.why: Owner-private local install; evidence files may be shared.
decisions.tradeoffs: Slightly more custom code (templates, in-container decryption)

decisions.decision: Stop the worker before the runtimes in stop.py.
decisions.why: Prevent the worker's desired-state reconciliation from restarting bots during shutdown.
decisions.alternatives: docker compose stop only (would not stop supervisor-owned runtimes)

decisions.decision: Acceptance drivers persist a proof manifest before mutation and refuse to re-run setup when it exists.
decisions.why: Avoid duplicate fixtures and duplicate real effects; resume instead of resubmitting.

decisions.decision: Tests run in a separate hermbot_test database inside a pinned tools container.
decisions.why: Product DB isolation; no host toolchain needed.
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires Docker and image build each run

decisions.decision: Failure injection in phase3_recovery_driver validates container labels and limits targets to researcher/writer.

invariants.text: .env is created with mode 0600 and never overwritten by configure.py.
Existing VAPID private key is never replaced.
Audits require zero failures/errors in backend.xml and no unsettled tasks/operations.

failures.text: Historical audits encode old image tags/runtime counts and fail on the current phase4 stack; treat them as records, not health checks.
Recovery driver is finite (1800s) and must be stopped after the intended checks; unknown signal actions raise.
If .env is missing, compose aborts with 'Run scripts/configure.py' / 'Run scripts/upgrade_config.py'.

security.text: Secrets are decrypted only inside app/worker containers (backend.secrets.decrypt) for drivers that need them; host scripts only read OWNER_TOKEN.
phase3_audit scans product tables and every API response for a secure-input canary to prove secrets never persisted.
event_provider_acceptance never approves: canaries wait for an actual human review decision.

In-chat reviews: ApprovalCard Allow once / Deny / Cancel review (POST /approvals/{id} with expected_payload_hash), Edit draft (PUT creates a new approval), Edit proposal (PUT /proposals/{id}); secure input reviews direct the owner to the computer.
Questions: InputCard text or choice answers via POST /input-requests/{id}/answer with expected_question_hash.
Reviews/questions are hidden once expired or when their task settled/cancelling/past deadline.
Outputs tab lists conversation artifacts (chat.artifacts) and opens them in the Library at that id.

Library: search by name/text, scope by conversation, 50 per page; upload (<=10MB base64) or import link; detail shows version/size/source/task/SHA-256; preview by content type; Download via /api/v1/artifacts/{id}?download=true.
Versions: 'Add new version' uploads with previous_id; version selector switches selection.
Shares: share selected version with a conversation, revoke share; note that admitted tasks keep their explicit grants.
Use in this conversation: shares then attaches as artifact_ids to the next message (max 10).
Search prior work: GET /api/v1/history/search; result click navigates to the conversation.
Open from chat header (Memory & skills) or 'Save as skill' on a completed work item (loads /tasks/{id}/skill-draft).
Curated memory: 'User profile' and 'Personal notes' targets; edit with character limit; empty content removes.

Skills: filter, enable/disable (POST .../enabled with expected_revision), open content (bundled read-only), create new from template, import SKILL.md (renamed hermbot-*), save with expected_hash and optional enable.
Saved versions load as drafts; saving creates a new version against the current native hash.
All edits disabled until the runtime is active and running; notice that the runtime refreshes after save.
Workspace settings 'Permitted tools' (file, terminal, skills, memory, browser, computer_use) bound the per-teammate Tools checkboxes in BotEditor.
Enabled skills are a comma list with datalist of installed skills from GET /bots/{id}/skills (only when runtime running).
CapabilitySummary (Knowledge panel) shows availability per native tool or blocked_tools message, and assigned connections with action counts; notes connections keep native tools available.
Open from header Monitor icon or from a secure-input review ('Open computer for secure input').
Polls status (1.5s) and thumbnail (2s); Start computer when stopped.
Expand live view: noVNC RFB to wss/ws same-origin /api/v1/bots/{id}/computer/ws, scaleViewport, view-only unless this session holds input-ready human control; reconnect button after disconnect.
Take over / Reclaim / Confirm control and Hand back (force when another session holds it) via POST computer/control; Stop computer disabled during human control; Open browser only when in control.

Secure input field clears immediately, first POSTs the teaching-private-input privacy barrier (aborting with an error if refused), then types characters via RFB.sendKey into the same still-current connection; Enter/Tab/Escape helpers.

security.text: The secret value never transits the REST API or chat; it is sent as keystrokes over the authenticated live connection and the local state is cleared. Before typing, the UI awaits a value-free POST /api/v1/bots/{id}/teaching-private-input so any teaching recording is paused first, and aborts if that call fails.

logic.step: Connections tab: cards per connection (provider, status, account, assigned teammates, action count, error); Edit access, Connect/Reconnect (OAuth redirect), Use access token, Discover MCP tools, Revoke.
Add/Edit connection: provider google/slack/github/mcp (MCP needs HTTPS endpoint), teammates, permitted actions (mutation actions marked 'reviewed change'), per-action resource allow lists.
OAuth setup tab: client id/secret per provider and displayed callback URL.
Permissions tab: standing permission for one bot + action + exact resource with expiry hours and max uses; revoke.
Activity tab: operations with exact arguments/result receipt; uncertain/unresolved can be reconciled with provider evidence.
Reviews of connector actions render a readable ConnectorPreview and structured ConnectorDraftFields editor; workspace 'Connected app actions' mode requested vs review.
Entry: sidebar Routines or composer clock button (pre-fills instructions from draft; disabled with attachments, threads, coordination or no provider).

Editor: name, results conversation + teammate, optional team coordination grant, instructions, schedule kind once/interval/daily/weekdays/weekly/monthly with timezone, expected results (report/artifact/connector_effect/execution_check/native_effect), inputs, budget, start window, catch-up skip/latest, max runs per UTC day, information window since_success.
Live 'Next occurrences' preview via POST /routines/preview (350ms debounce); save blocked on preview error or no next occurrence when enabled.
List shows state, schedule text, next run, last run, errors and scheduler staleness (>180s); actions Edit, History, Run now, Pause/Resume, Pause and stop current run, Delete (archive, confirm).
History lists runs with status/origin/revision/output; Open run and results navigates to the conversation thread; Stop current run.
Routines panel 'Events' mode hosts EventTriggers with views triggers, sources, edit, source-edit, history, deliveries.

Sources: Slack (Socket Mode app token), GitHub (poll or signed webhook), Google Drive/Calendar/Gmail (poll), generic signed webhook (Standard Webhooks headers); credential saved via /secrets with optional previous-key overlap; actions check/pause/archive/resync.

Trigger editor: source, event types, AND conditions (equals/contains/starts_with on provider-specific fields), teammate/conversation, coordination, instructions, expected results with optional 'request this action for every occurrence', limits (budget, start delay, runs/day, max pending), ignore bot-origin events, coalescing for latest-state types.
Sample-event check via POST /event-triggers/preview (no work started).

History: work occurrences with event counts and Open/Stop; received events with matched/ignored reason and expandable context; Deliveries log with duplicate counts and Retry recording for recording_failed.

Workspace settings > Grants: create standing grant (manager, targets, operations incl. lifecycle ones marked owner-approval, expiry hours, new-bot budget, per-bot memory/CPU caps); list unexpired/standing grants with revoke-and-stop.
Lifecycle proposals arrive as approvals of kind 'lifecycle' showing configuration/before/resources/affected tasks; 'Edit proposal' replaces it via PUT /api/v1/proposals/{id}.
TaskInspector lists teammate proposals and the owner-issued authority (targets/operations/expiry).
Recurring management for routines/triggers uses RecurringManagement to pick or create a delegate standing grant.

Owner menu > Notifications opens settings (10s poll) showing worker health, browser enablement, categories (questions/reviews/results/problems), quiet hours with IANA timezone, and registered browsers.

Enable this browser: checks secure context/Push support/configured keys/permission; requests permission in the click gesture; registers /sw.js; subscribes with the VAPID public key; POSTs the subscription with key_id; turns push_enabled on.
Service worker shows a generic notification and opens /?attention=<id> on click; the app opens the Attention panel at that item.
Disable a device (DELETE subscription) and sign out both clear the local push subscription.

security.text: Notification text is always generic; payload contents are not displayed and target is validated to a UUID-like id or 'inbox' before building the URL.

logic.step: Login screen asks for the owner token from .env (password field); POST /api/v1/session with Authorization Bearer; the token is discarded from component state.
All requests use same-origin cookies; 401 triggers global reset to login (SSE closed, query cache and idempotency keys cleared).
Sign out: DELETE /api/v1/session, clear browser push, close SSE, clear caches.
Secrets are write-only in UI: provider api_key, OAuth client secret, connection tokens, event source credentials use password inputs with autocomplete off/new-password and are cleared after save.
Workspace settings (timezone, default provider, limits, permitted tools, decision provider, connected app action mode) via GET/PUT /api/v1/settings.
Computer panel shows lease holder and 'Waiting for in-flight work to settle' until input_ready; 'Bot tools and new dispatch remain paused until handback' when admission_paused.
Status label waiting_computer = 'Waiting for computer handback'; CapabilitySummary asks to hand back the computer; TaskActivity shows tool.admitted 'admitted; waiting to start'.
phase3_inflight.py proves takeover waits for a running foreground tool (>4s) and the effect runs once after handback; phase3_recovery_driver injects worker pause/restart and runtime recreation.
scripts/check.py runs ruff + pytest in hermbot-tools against hermbot_test and writes test-results/backend.xml, which every audit reads for test counts/failures.
Audit scripts cross-check saved test-results evidence JSON against live API state and Docker inspection; acceptance drivers create fixtures through the owner API and write proof manifests.
UI is exercised by Playwright scripts in tests/browser (e.g. ui-regressions, work-items, routines, event-triggers, phase3-computer), referenced by audits via test-results JSON.

steps.text: Owner types in the composer; send() builds {intent:'auto', bot_id, conversation_id, prompt, grant_id | managed_bot_ids(+management_operations), attachment_ids, artifact_ids, reply_to_message_id, mention_bot_ids}.
Idempotency-Key is reused while the payload fingerprint is unchanged (safe resubmission after a network failure); POST /api/v1/messages.
On success the draft is cleared only if the same conversation/thread is still active; state and chat queries are invalidated.
Response row shows 'Understanding your message' during automatic intake; on failure 'Retry interpretation'.
SSE /api/v1/events delivers 'update' rows: task.started resets and message.delta appends streamed text; each event triggers a debounced refetch of state/chat/attention.
Work panel renders the work item (status, assignments, required results progress, outputs) and controls (inspect, redirect, stop, retry, continue).
Reviews and questions raised by the run appear inline (ApprovalCard/InputCard) and in Attention.
When the task settles the transcript refetch shows the bot's final message, outcomes show accepted/fulfilled with evidence strength, and Outputs lists published artifacts.
TaskInspector shows tree, executions, assessments and events by polling GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}.
A pending connector approval (kind 'connector') renders ApprovalCard with ConnectorPreview of action and arguments, recipient display name resolved from the bound outcome.
Owner decides Allow once / Deny / Cancel review: POST /api/v1/approvals/{id} {decision, expected_payload_hash}.
Or Edit draft: structured fields edit arguments; mutate PUT /api/v1/approvals/{id} creates a replacement approval (old one cannot authorize).
While dispatching, task label shows 'Applying approved change' / 'Waiting for application' / 'Check application outcome'.
Uncertain/unresolved connector state shows 'Review application outcome' in chat and on the work card, blocking retry/continue, linking to Connections > Activity.
Activity tab shows exact arguments and receipt; owner records succeeded/failed/unresolved with provider evidence via POST /api/v1/connector-operations/{id}/reconcile.
Standing permissions (one bot, action, exact resource, expiry, max uses) let matching actions proceed without per-action review.
Owner creates a routine (or from composer draft): schedule preview via POST /api/v1/routines/preview; save via mutate POST /api/v1/routines (create) or PUT /api/v1/routines/{id}.
Routine list (5s) shows next run, last run status/reason and warns when the scheduler last_tick_at is older than 3 minutes.
Run now / Pause / Resume / Pause and stop / Delete call mutate POST /api/v1/routines/{id}/{action} with expected_revision; Run now shows the admission reason if skipped.
History (5s) lists runs (scheduled/manual origin, revision, output); Open run and results jumps to the conversation thread; Stop current run stops the task.

Owner enables push: permission request in the click gesture, register /sw.js (scope '/'), PushManager.subscribe with VAPID public key, POST /api/v1/notifications/subscriptions {endpoint, keys, key_id, label}.
Push service delivers to the service worker; it validates target, shows fixed generic text with tag and icon, renotify false.
notificationclick focuses/navigates an existing same-origin window or opens /?attention=<id|inbox>.
App reads ?attention on load and opens the Attention panel with that item selected; closing removes the query param.
In-app attention counts refresh every 5s and after each SSE event regardless of push.
On load the app probes GET /api/v1/state; success means a valid session cookie exists.
Otherwise the login card asks for the owner token and POSTs /api/v1/session with Authorization: Bearer <token>; the token is cleared from state on success.
All subsequent fetches, the EventSource and the noVNC WebSocket rely on the same-origin session cookie.
Any 401 dispatches 'hermbot-session-expired': the app closes SSE, clears the query cache and idempotency keys and returns to login.
Sign out: DELETE /api/v1/session, unsubscribe local push and close notifications, reset UI state.
Owner picks files in the composer: max 10 total, 10MB each; read as base64 with MIME overrides for md/csv/py/json/txt.
Each file: mutate POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/attachments {name, content_type, content_base64} with Idempotency-Key; chips added only if the same conversation is still active.
Library files can instead be shared to the conversation and attached as artifact_ids.
Message submission carries attachment_ids/artifact_ids; backend installs them into the bot workspace before execution.
Message chips link to GET /api/v1/attachments/{id}; teammate briefs show shared attachment/file counts.

discrepancies.text: README says the sidebar lists share one scroll area 'with File library and owner controls kept visible below it'; code moved File library into the owner popover menu and the .library-nav CSS is now dead.
README calls the sidebar heading 'Your team'; UI label is 'Your teammates'.
Dead component: OperationNotice is exported from Management.tsx but never imported.
Dead CSS selectors with no matching className in any component: .library-nav, .private, .revoke, .eyebrow, .schedule-preview.

Tailwind @source only lists 7 of 18 TSX files (omits Routines, EventTriggers, Attention, Notifications, etc.); harmless today because components use hand-written classes, but any Tailwind utility added there would be silently missing.

web/dist is a stale Oct 6 build (no attention/notifications/library/connections/event-trigger code, Inter font) left in the tree; it is git/docker-ignored and the image rebuilds the UI, so it is never served.
Vite dev proxy forwards /api without ws:true, so the noVNC WebSocket would not work under `npm run dev`; no compose service runs the dev server (production serves the SPA from the API).
Providers tab always prints 'key configured' even though Provider has key_configured?: boolean.
Reaction chips always render '<emoji> 1' and are keyed by emoji, so several authors reacting with the same emoji produce duplicate React keys and wrong counts.
ApprovalCard is declared inside App, so it is a new component type on every App render (forces remount each render; also reused by Attention via renderReview).

EventSource is created once (guarded by source.current) and never recreated if the browser closes it permanently (non-200/invalid response); live streaming text stops while the 5s polling fallback keeps state current until reload or re-login.

Sign-out awaits DELETE /api/v1/session before local cleanup; if that request throws (e.g. network error) push unsubscribe and state reset are skipped. A 401 instead goes through the expiry handler, which does not call clearBrowserPush.
UI hard-codes seed bot ids as defaults (composer target 'researcher', group members researcher/writer/reviewer, grant manager 'reviewer') although bots are dynamic.
OutcomeActions does not invalidate any query after drop/reconcile; the card updates only after the SSE-triggered refetch or the 5s state poll.

Backend routes with no UI caller: GET /api/v1/bots, GET /api/v1/bot-operations (scripts only), GET /api/v1/grants, GET /api/v1/owner-sessions, DELETE /api/v1/owner-sessions/{id}, DELETE /api/v1/conversations/{id}, POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/restore, POST /api/v1/tasks (legacy; scripts only), GET /api/v1/conversations/{id}/runtime-history/{bot_id} (skills_tools_audit only), POST /api/v1/work-items/messages (group_work_history only). Owner session listing/revocation has no UI.

Historical audit scripts hard-code superseded expectations (phase2_audit: image hermbot-hermes:phase2 and exactly 5 runtimes; phase3_audit: /health phase 3 and image hermbot-hermes:phase3) while compose now builds hermbot-hermes:phase4; they would fail against the current stack.

event_trigger_acceptance.py browser-cleanup stage deletes rows directly from event_trigger_revisions, event_trigger_definitions, messages and event_sources, bypassing API invariants; event_provider_acceptance.reconcile_creation UPDATEs trigger_resource_versions and inserts events directly.

Several ops/acceptance scripts embed workspace-specific fixture identifiers (conversation/task/routine UUIDs, a GitHub test repo, Slack #test, the owner's own mailbox) so they are not reusable on another installation.

configure.py does not create PUBLIC_URL or VAPID_* entries; PUBLIC_URL comes from upgrade_config.py or the compose default and VAPID keys from notification_setup.py (README documents both). notification_setup.py resolves .env relative to the current directory unlike the other scripts.
scripts/__pycache__ contains compiled bytecode for event_provider_acceptance, event_trigger_acceptance and group_work_history (run as modules inside the container with the repo mounted).

topology.text: The React SPA is compiled in the api image (node stage: npm ci, tsc -b, vite build) and served by the same FastAPI process via StaticFiles at '/' after all API routes, so UI and API share one origin (127.0.0.1:8780).

Browser-facing channels: JSON REST (/api/v1/*), one SSE stream (/api/v1/events), a per-bot noVNC WebSocket (/api/v1/bots/{id}/computer/ws), Web Push via the browser vendor push service to /sw.js, and browser navigation for OAuth callbacks.

observability.text: UI surfaces server-side health: worker check-in for notifications, routine scheduler staleness (>180s), event source status/gaps/errors, runtime_error per bot, provisioning failures, assessment status, last runtime contact/progress per task.
Recent activity panel shows the last 6 non-delta events for the active conversation from a 20-event in-memory buffer.

recovery.text: UI is stateless with respect to work: closing the browser leaves runs going; on reconnect the SPA reloads /state and conversation history, and EventSource reconnects using Last-Event-ID; SSE onopen triggers a full refetch.
Lost responses to mutations are safe to retry from the UI because the Idempotency-Key is kept per request fingerprint until success.

concurrency.text: Optimistic concurrency fields are threaded from UI state into every edit: expected_revision (bots, routines, triggers, sources, connections, providers, outcomes, skill enable), expected_hash (knowledge), expected_payload_hash (approvals), expected_input_hash (queued instructions), expected_question_hash (answers), attention item version.
Stale async results are dropped via generation counters (chat scope, usePanelScope).

security.text: Owner token is only typed once to mint an HttpOnly session cookie; the SPA never stores it. Secrets entered in the UI are write-only and cleared after submit.
Backend rejects non-GET requests whose Origin host differs and the computer WebSocket checks Origin; the SPA is same-origin so it passes, other sites cannot drive it.
Push notifications never reveal content; the service worker ignores payload text and validates the deep-link target.

production-path.text: Web Push and secure browser APIs need a secure context: localhost works on the host; LAN HTTP access from a phone does not, and the UI states this.

tradeoffs.decision: SSE events only invalidate queries instead of patching client state
tradeoffs.benefit: Server stays the single source of truth; no client reducer to keep consistent with dozens of event kinds
tradeoffs.cost: Each burst of events refetches the large /state payload (debounced to 250ms) in addition to 5s polling

tradeoffs.benefit: Simple consistency across sidebar, chat, work panel and reviews
tradeoffs.cost: Payload grows with all tasks/work items/approvals; filtering happens client-side

tradeoffs.decision: Base64 JSON uploads (attachments, library) instead of multipart
tradeoffs.benefit: Same JSON + Idempotency-Key mutate path for all writes
tradeoffs.cost: ~33% size overhead and whole-file memory buffering; client caps files at 10MB

unknowns.text: Whether the backend deduplicates or records failed (4xx) responses under an Idempotency-Key; the UI reuses the same key after an HTTP error for an identical body.
